recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Given the decoded PowerShell payload is a routine `git diff --stat HEAD` command, it would be prudent to confirm that the node.js process invoking it originates from an approved internal package and that its source code has not been tampered with. A quick audit of the @anthropic‑ai/claude-code repository hash against the version installed in the user’s npm cache can provide assurance that the CLI script is legitimate.

Even though no malicious domains were resolved, it remains useful to keep an eye on outbound DNS queries from the same process for any future anomalies. A lightweight monitoring rule that flags any subsequent encoded PowerShell executions or unexpected network connections from node.exe would help catch a potential pivot if the attacker later injects more sophisticated payloads.

Because the event was captured by Sysmon, you might want to enable additional Sysmon logging (e.g., ProcessCommandLine and FileCreateTime) for the node.exe binary. This will give you richer context should another encoded command surface, allowing you to correlate it with user activity or scheduled tasks.

Finally, consider adding a brief reminder in your internal dev‑ops playbook that any use of `powershell -EncodedCommand` should be logged and reviewed, even when the payload appears benign. This will reinforce a culture of vigilance without generating unnecessary noise.
